description: Implements FORMULATION.md section 6's opportunity formula Omega_k = w_D*D_k - w_K*K_k + w_Sigma*Sigma_k, combining demand, competition and simplicity z-scores, restricted to archetypes clearing the minimum cluster size.
signature: def build_opportunity_matrix(demand: pd.DataFrame, competition: pd.DataFrame, simplicity: pd.DataFrame, params: AnalysisParams) -> pd.DataFrame
docstring:
Assemble the opportunity matrix.

Args:
    demand: compute_demand's output.
    competition: compute_competition_density's output.
    simplicity: A DataFrame indexed by cluster_id with a median_complexity column (median complexity_score of the archetype's windowed games, from apply_simplicity_filter's input population, i.e. computed by whichever caller -- run_analysis -- joins the buildable/full frame per archetype; this function receives it pre-computed).
    params: AnalysisParams.opportunity_weights, min_cluster_size.

Returns:
    A DataFrame with columns cluster_id, label, n_games, demand_z, competition_z, simplicity_z, opportunity_score, median_estimated_sales_mid, median_complexity, releases_in_window -- restricted to archetypes present in ALL THREE input frames with n_games >= params.min_cluster_size. Sigma_k = z(1 - median_complexity) is computed here (the '1 -' inversion, since LOWER complexity should contribute POSITIVELY to simplicity_z, per FORMULATION.md's Sigma_k formula) before calling compute_zscore. Ties in opportunity_score are broken by cluster_id ascending, per the module's own invariant.
preconditions: demand, competition and simplicity share a common cluster_id indexing scheme (all three derived from the same cluster_tags call for this run)
postconditions: Every returned row has n_games >= params.min_cluster_size

z-scores are computed only over the scored (i.e. already min_cluster_size-filtered) population, per the module's own invariant 'z-scores are computed over the scored cluster population of the same run and are therefore comparable within a run but not across runs'
Result is sorted by opportunity_score descending, ties by cluster_id ascending

edge_cases.input: An archetype present in demand and competition but with n_games < min_cluster_size
edge_cases.expected_behavior: excluded from the returned matrix entirely, not scored with a low/null value -- it is reported separately by run_analysis via AnalysisReport.clusters_below_min_size, not as a matrix row

compute_zscore's zero-variance guard applies (a single-row z-score population trivially has zero variance for every column), so demand_z=competition_z=simplicity_z=0 and opportunity_score=0 for that sole archetype -- reported, per the module's own edge case 'A single archetype dominating the candidate set -> reported, since a near-degenerate clustering invalidates comparison'

edge_cases.input: An archetype missing from one of the three input frames (e.g. present in demand but not competition, which should not normally happen since both are computed from the same assignments)
edge_cases.expected_behavior: excluded from the result via an inner join across the three frames -- treated as a data-consistency issue worth a warning event from the caller, not silently included with a partial/NaN score

unit_tests.name: test_reproduces_hand_computed_zscores_and_combination
unit_tests.description: A synthetic set of archetypes with known demand/competition/simplicity values reproduces the hand-computed z-scores and weighted combination exactly, per the module's own testing requirement.
unit_tests.expected: matches hand computation to floating-point tolerance

unit_tests.name: test_zero_variance_inputs_produce_zero_not_nan
unit_tests.description: Identical demand values across all scored archetypes produce demand_z=0 for all, not NaN, per the module's own testing requirement.

unit_tests.name: test_below_min_size_excluded_from_scoring
unit_tests.description: An archetype with n_games below min_cluster_size does not appear in the returned matrix.

unit_tests.name: test_ties_broken_by_cluster_id
unit_tests.description: Two archetypes with identical opportunity_score are ordered by cluster_id ascending.
